subject: OrbitEdge - Dedicated capacity: request for traffic decomposition and sizing inputs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Ellis Grant <ellis@orbitedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrbitEdge - Dedicated capacity: request for traffic decomposition and sizing inputs

Hi Ellis —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To prepare a tight Dedicated proposal (sizing, sku mix, and burst plan) we need a short traffic decomposition so our pre-sales model can map to GPU capacity and caching strategy. Can you share the following for a representative 24h period and for your three main workflows (chat support, document summarization, codegen):

- 1hr and 24hr request counts and p95/p99 request arrival rates (per workflow)
- Typical prompt token distribution (median, p90, p99) and typical response token distribution
- Average prompt+response tokens per request and percent of responses > 1k tokens
- Session lifetime / average connection duration and whether you use streaming or chunked responses
- Peak concurrent active sessions and expected burst windows (start/end times + multiplier)
- Any long-polling / websocket session patterns vs short HTTP calls
- Whether responses contain binary blobs (images/base64) or large attachments embedded inline

If you can’t export token counts, character counts are OK for a first pass — just flag which they are. Attaching a quick intake template (pre-sales-sizer-template.xlsx) you can drop samples into.

Goal: propose a committed pool and a burst policy that hits your 99th latency SLO while minimizing committed GPU-months. Would you be able to share a sanitized 24h request sample (CSV or NDJSON) and a short prompt catalog by EOD tomorrow?

I’ll loop Marissa and Tessa on GPU SKU recommendations once we see the samples.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pre-sales-sizer-template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Ellis Grant <ellis@orbitedge.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@orbitedge.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@orbitedge.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitEdge - Dedicated capacity: request for traffic decomposition and sizing inputs

Hi Aditya —

Appreciate the checklist. I pulled together a short summary and attached a 24-hour sample (orbitedge_traffic_sample.csv) plus a prompt catalog for the three workflows. Quick highlights from our telemetry (last 30 days, representative weekday):

- Chat support: 18k req/day, avg arrival rate 0.21 rps sustained, p95 arrival bursts to 1.6 rps; median prompt 45 tokens, p90 160, p99 420; median response 80 tokens, p90 350
- Document summarization: 4.2k req/day, batched primarily via HTTP batch job windows (02:00–04:00 UTC), avg prompt 250 tokens, avg response 1,200 tokens; 12% responses >1k tokens
- Codegen (internal dev tools): 2.6k req/day, sporadic bursts around deploys, median prompt 120 tokens, median response 300 tokens, p99 response ~2,200 tokens (large code dumps)

Session pattern: chat uses streaming websocket connections with average session duration 4.2 minutes; other workflows are short HTTP calls (3–45s). Peak concurrent sessions observed: ~420 active websockets around 15:30 PDT (support shift change). Burst window: typical day has a 3x multiplier for ~20–30 minutes during post-deploy runs.

Notes/assumptions: token counts above are already tokenized using tiktoken-like split (we export token counts). Responses do not include inline base64 images; attachments are handed out as separate URLs.

We’re considering a starting committed run of 16 GPUs but would like your recommendation (sku mix / autoscale to handle 3x bursts) and an estimate of monthly committed cost vs target p99 latency (50–150ms per token).

I’ve attached orbitedge_traffic_sample.csv and prompt_catalog.pdf. Procurement wants a short list of required contract terms and a draft SLA if possible.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call tomorrow morning PT.

—Ellis
Ellis Grant
Head of Platform
OrbitEdge

Attachments: orbitedge_traffic_sample.csv, prompt_catalog.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Ellis Grant <ellis@orbitedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 12:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitEdge - Dedicated capacity: request for traffic decomposition and sizing inputs

Ellis —

This is great — thank you. A few clarifying asks so our sizing maps cleanly to invoice-able units:

- Confirm token counts are for the same encoding (you noted tiktoken-like; please confirm model family if known)
- For the document summarization workflow: are the 1,200-token responses produced in single-stream responses or chunked streams? If chunked, what is the average chunk size?
- For codegen p99 large responses (~2,200 tokens): are these frequently streamed or do you keep whole response in memory before returning? This affects our KV cache sizing and memory planning.
- Please include a sample request JSON for each workflow if you can (headers, approximate request size, and any metadata flags that affect route selection).

Operational note: based on the sketch above I want to propose a mixed reserved pool (some H100-class for high-throughput batched summarization and A100-class for latency-sensitive streaming chat). We can also propose an autoscale/burst policy that spins up an additional set of instances for sustained >2x load for >10 minutes.

I attached a small example of the specific CSV columns we need (pre-sales-sizer-template.xlsx). If you can drop the sample into that and share, I’ll produce a first-pass SKU & latency mapping plus cost comparison (committed vs on-demand).

Also, procurement: if you can send your standard PO/terms and a preferred billing cadence that’ll help.

Best,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Looping in a quick sizing note — feel free to paste this into the proposal: 

- Recommended starter pool: 8 x A100-80GB (latency-sensitive chat + codegen p95) + 4 x H100-80GB (batched summarization and heavy throughput jobs)
- Autoscale policy: burst layer of up to +12 nodes (mix of smaller SKUs) triggered on sustained >2x arrival rate for >10 minutes
- KV cache: assume warm-cache hit-rate of 70% for chat; plan for cold-warm transitions during shift changes
- Quantization: recommend we include a 4/8-bit quantization option for the summarization model to reduce GPU memory and increase density — add as alternative pricing line item

I’ll take the first pass at an estimated committed monthly cost and include a fallback on-demand cost for the initial 3 months. Aditya — once they share the sample CSV I’ll model occupancy and token-econ.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Aditya / Marissa —

Thanks — I dropped the sample CSV and prompt catalog in your Drive link and confirmed tokenization with our infra team (we’re using tiktoken-cl100k-like encoding). Confirming the following:

- Document summarization responses are streamed (chunked) — avg chunk ~512 tokens; client reassembles.
- Codegen large responses are returned as a single payload (we can change this if it simplifies memory footprint).
- No inline base64 blobs.

We’re available for a 45-min call Thu 09:00–10:00 PT or Fri 10:30–11:15 PT to review your first-pass sizing. Procurement attached a short guide (procurement-instructions.pdf) with their PO template and compliance contact.

Please include a short SLA draft and proposed start-of-service date (we’re targeting 2029-07-01).

Ellis
